chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who divorces his wife, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'She inherits him and he inherits her as long as he has the right of return (raj'ah) over her.'
ai.seo_question: Does a divorced wife inherit her husband during the waiting period?
ai.summary: Reported by the prominent jurist Zurarah from Imam al-Baqir, this hadith clarifies that the marital bond remains intact during the 'iddah of a revocable divorce, thereby preserving mutual inheritance rights. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the dissolution of marriage is not immediate upon pronouncement but is finalized only after the 'iddah concludes or a formal revocation occurs.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara who said,
‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the man who divorces the wife. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She would inherit him and he would inherit her for as long as he has the right to go back to her’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who has narrated the following: “
I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who divorces his wife. He (the Imam) said, ‘She inherits him and he inherits her as long as he has the right to go back to her.’”
